claims.notes: Verified by local git refs and package metadata without modifying the checkout.
claims.statement: The appropriate current baseline for the next-version investigation is origin/master d5096b7 (package version 0.9.6), not the clean but six-commit-behind local master.

claims.notes: O005 should independently confirm the release-gate implication before roadmap promotion.
claims.statement: The current tarball passes its available local R package checks, but those checks do not exercise a test suite or packaged vignettes because neither is present in the built package.

claims.notes: Verified through local refs and a remote API read.
claims.statement: The audited revision d5096b7 was the live GitHub master as of 2026-08-30.

claims.notes: Candidate P0/P1 coordinate defect for O005.
claims.statement: The public global origin parameters are not applied consistently, so nonzero x0/y0 can reverse the two sides and y0 is ignored.

claims.notes: Candidate P1 API-default defect for O005.
claims.statement: The new geom_nodemarquee() wrapper's default invocation fails its required label aesthetic and is inconsistent with geom_tipmarquee().

claims.notes: Candidate P1 input-contract defect for O005.
claims.statement: Metadata key normalization is inconsistent with the package's own examples, so numeric keys can fail before geometry is returned.

claims.notes: Candidate P2 API cleanup item for O005.
claims.statement: The exported stat_bipnet() defaults are internally inconsistent for common inherited mappings and non-interaction types.

claims.notes: Candidate P2 low-level API correction.
claims.statement: compute_interaction_coords() enforces an optional-column assumption through strict selection, contradicting its public input contract.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 correctness defect for O005.
claims.statement: Interaction group IDs are not injective, so distinct ribbons can be merged into one polygon group and rendered incorrectly.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 input defect for O005.
claims.statement: The documented .rowname contract and unnamed-matrix handling in to_longer() are broken, causing errors or invalid identifiers.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 correctness defect for O005.
claims.statement: Duplicate row-column observations are not normalized before matrix construction, so a supported-looking long input can fail before the intended aggregation step.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 edge-case defect for O005.
claims.statement: Height-adjustment helpers do not preserve their return schema for equal or singleton partitions, exposing NULL or infinite gaps through public layout APIs.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 phylogeny-alignment defect for O005.
claims.statement: Tip-position normalization can include internal nodes and align a network ID to the wrong y coordinate when labels collide.

claims.notes: Candidate P0 data-integrity defect for O005.
claims.statement: Unvalidated metadata cardinality can silently multiply boxes and interaction vertices, corrupting geometry and mapped attributes.

claims.notes: Candidate P1 release-engineering claim for O005.
claims.statement: A testthat/CI/visual-regression release gate and explicit minimum dependency versions are prerequisite structural work for the next release.

claims.notes: O005 must distinguish necessary architecture from stylistic preference and preserve 0.x compatibility.
claims.statement: After correctness is stabilized, the package should introduce a validated layout object and staged lifecycle cleanup instead of expanding the current low-level API surface.

claims.notes: O005 should challenge default mismatch policy and distinguish bug fixes from new API.
claims.statement: A pure input-normalization and tree/network ID-reconciliation layer is a Must for the next version because the current workflow delegates correctness-critical ordering and mismatch handling to users.

claims.notes: O005 should test whether this belongs in the immediate release after correctness gates.
claims.statement: A thin high-level composer backed by one shared validated layout is a Must-level usability feature, provided it returns editable components and does not become a monolith.

claims.notes: External size semantics require explicit relative/absolute scaling rules.
claims.statement: Interaction-level metadata and optional independent node sizes are Should-level extensions, while a dedicated bipartite adapter and duplicated network-analysis methods are unnecessary.

claims.notes: Actual adapter priority depends on whether target users are microbiome-focused or general ecological-network users.
claims.statement: Broader treeio-compatible input is a Should, but phyloseq and TreeSummarizedExperiment adapters are Could-level optional converters after the canonical data model stabilizes.

claims.notes: Acceptance must preserve topology, branch lengths, labels, and return before/after crossing scores.
claims.statement: Crossing minimization is a valuable Should-level feature, but it should follow correctness, shared layout, and deterministic baseline ordering rather than enter the immediate stabilization release.

claims.notes: Use tuple-safe grouping and a regression test.
claims.statement: Distinct interaction tuples can collapse to one polygon group, silently corrupting the scientific visualization; this is a P0 release blocker.

claims.notes: Validate uniqueness and join relationship before geometry construction.
claims.statement: Duplicate metadata keys silently multiply boxes and vertices, corrupting geometry and attributes; this is a P0 release blocker.

claims.notes: Standard named-matrix default calls still work, so it is not P0.
claims.statement: to_longer() rowname handling and unnamed matrices violate the public input contract; this is a verified P1 defect.

claims.notes: The new input contract must make aggregation versus rejection explicit.
claims.statement: Duplicate long-form cells fail before the intended aggregation step and produce an empty layer with a warning; this is a verified P1 defect.

claims.notes: Main stat and constructor default adjustment to FALSE, limiting scope.
claims.statement: Equal or singleton partition height adjustment can expose NULL or infinite gaps; this is a verified P1 opt-in layout defect.

claims.notes: Filter isTip before label/y normalization.
claims.statement: Tip normalization can include an internal node when labels collide and produce a wrong y target; this is a verified but scoped P1 defect.

claims.notes: The main stat hardcodes zero origin, so ordinary plots are not affected.
claims.statement: Nonzero x0/y0 values are not propagated consistently through public layout coordinates; this is a verified P1 low-level API defect.

claims.notes: Explicit aes(label = label) is a workaround.
claims.statement: geom_nodemarquee() fails its natural default invocation because label is omitted; this is a verified P1 wrapper-default defect.

claims.notes: Normalize both sides and validate key existence and uniqueness.
claims.statement: Numeric metadata keys shown in package examples can fail type-sensitive joins; this is a verified P1 input-normalization defect.

claims.notes: Visual snapshots should be scoped; exact dependency floors still require version-matrix checks.
claims.statement: A testthat plus CI correctness gate covering the verified P0/P1 cases is a Must before the next release.

claims.notes: The exact function/class boundary and mismatch default remain design choices.
claims.statement: Validated canonical normalization for identifiers, types, duplicate cells, metadata cardinality, and tree-tip matching is a Must-level structural change.

claims.notes: The composer return contract and optional composition dependency remain unresolved.
claims.statement: One shared validated layout should replace per-layer recomputation as a Must-level architectural boundary; a separate high-level composer remains a later Should.

claims.notes: Reconsider when a representative workflow, dataset, and acceptance criterion exist.
claims.statement: Interaction metadata, external node sizes, broader adapters, and crossing optimization lack package-specific demand or benchmarks and should not enter the immediate release scope.

claims.notes: No new visualization feature should precede the release-blocking fixes.
claims.statement: The next release should be a 0.9.7 stabilization release limited to regression infrastructure, the verified P0/P1 fixes, explicit input policies, and release checks.

claims.notes: Exact class/function names and composer dependency remain design choices.
claims.statement: A subsequent 0.10.0 should introduce a canonical normalized input boundary and one reusable layout object, route existing layers through it with compatibility shims, and treat a high-level tree-network composer as a late Should item.

claims.notes: Promote only with representative workflows, datasets, benchmarks, and acceptance criteria.
claims.statement: Interaction metadata, independent node abundance, treeio/phyloseq/TSE adapters, crossing optimization, curved ribbons, and sparse backends should remain evidence-gated backlog rather than immediate release scope.

claims.notes: Avoid mixing a repository-wide style rewrite into the bug-fix diff.
claims.statement: Tidyverse-style modernization should be staged after correctness changes: align tests with R files, adopt base pipes internally, clarify errors and documentation, then deprecate legacy exports without immediate removal.

evidence.summary: git status and git log show clean local master 7d45947 is six commits behind origin/master d5096b7; the remote baseline adds marquee geoms and related package-check changes.

The baseline declares version 0.9.6, R >= 4.1.0, ggplot2/ggtree/tidyverse-component dependencies, and 28 exports spanning layout primitives, ggplot2 layers, tree helpers, marquee layers, and deprecated heterogeneous-data helpers.
origin/master contains no tests/ or .github/ paths. The vignettes directory is excluded by .Rbuildignore even though DESCRIPTION declares VignetteBuilder: quarto and Suggests: quarto.

evidence.locator: command:R CMD build --no-build-vignettes --no-manual . && R CMD check --no-manual --no-build-vignettes ggbipartite_0.9.6.tar.gz
evidence.summary: On R 4.6.0 arm64 macOS, the archived origin/master tarball builds and checks successfully with Status: OK; check reports INFO that quarto is required without any packaged vignettes. Repository network indexes were unavailable but did not affect local examples or loading checks.

Documented workflows cover abundance and binary bipartite layouts, manual metadata joins, manual tree/link/network composition, tip alignment, scientific-name/support formatting, marquee labels, and publication export examples.

The requested standards emphasize consistent snake_case naming, verb-led functions, two-space structural indentation, clear pipes, 80-column readability, meaningful errors, automated tests, explicit documentation, and reducing cognitive load through focused functions and unambiguous names.
A read-only GitHub API query on 2026-08-30 confirmed remote master still resolves to the locally tracked origin/master commit d5096b7.
I002 independently reproduced that (a,bc) and (ab,c) both become group abc and are consumed as one polygon drawing group.
I002 reproduced blank ggplot layers for adjust_box_height TRUE on a square network and NULL public gap fields when default gap zero makes both sides equal.
I002 independently reproduced that duplicate row-column observations fail in pivot_wider before aggregation and leave an empty layer.
With .x0=100 and .y0=100, row xmin is 100 but column xmin is 14.18 and both sides begin at y=0 because column x omits the origin and compute_box_coords calls omit y0.
ggtree(tree) + geom_nodemarquee() fails because label is absent from the default mapping, whereas explicitly mapping label succeeds and the analogous tip wrapper supplies label by default.
The documented integer metadata keys fail dplyr joins because only coordinate IDs are coerced to character; x$row is character while y$row remains integer.
stat_bipnet() defaults to inherit.aes FALSE and geom polygon regardless of type, so an ordinary inherited-aesthetic call lacks required aesthetics and type row lacks polygon x/y output.
The documentation treats interaction_size in box tables as optional, but strict negative selection errors when the column is absent.

evidence.locator: command:R CMD build and R CMD check origin/master tarball;command:quarto render README.qmd
evidence.summary: I002 independently confirmed tarball check and all Rd examples succeed, and the repository README renders; formal package checks still exclude all three vignettes and no tests exist.
Two distinct interactions (a,bc) and (ab,c) produce eight vertices but only one ggplot group because paste0(row, column) maps both to abc.
to_longer() hard-codes row after accepting a configurable .rowname; custom or NULL .rowname errors, while missing matrix dimnames can yield unusable factor IDs.
Duplicate long-form row-column observations reach pivot_wider before the package's aggregation helper, producing a list-column conversion failure and an empty ggplot layer with a computation warning.
calc_global_params() defaults to height adjustment, but equal row/column counts make adjust_box_height() return NULL gaps; singleton sides can also divide by n - 1 and return Inf.
extract_tip_positions() takes the generic label/y branch before inspecting isTip, so labeled internal nodes can be treated as tip targets; tree extraction logic is also duplicated.
Metadata keys are joined without uniqueness or relationship validation; a duplicate row key expands two row boxes to three and sixteen polygon vertices to twenty-four.
No tests or CI exist, and dependency floors are unspecified despite use of dplyr .by and ggplot2 linewidth APIs introduced in later releases.

The public surface mixes high- and low-level helpers, dot-prefixed helpers, a re-exported pipe, deprecated data-frame utilities, legacy aliases, and a misspelled public argument; one large stat file also duplicates tree/ggplot compatibility helpers and repeatedly recomputes layout.

The package exports layout and layer primitives but no single entry point for two trees plus a network; documented workflows manually build and align five panels and warn users about ID/order preparation.
ggtree/aplot document aligned tree-associated panels, while ggbipartite recalculates layout per layer and requires callers to compose tree/link/network components manually.

bipartite analysis and plotweb workflows accept ordinary matrices, while ggbipartite already accepts matrices and side metadata but has no interaction-metadata contract or independent node-size input.

ggbipartite tree support is inconsistent across helpers; treeio-compatible objects and TreeSummarizedExperiment rowTree/colTree match later interoperability needs better than making phyloseq a core dependency.
phytools cophylo, ape cophyloplot, and bipartite sorting establish topology-preserving rotation or ordering as standard methods for reducing link crossings.
Fresh-context reproduction found eight vertices but one group for two distinct tuple keys, confirming silent interaction-polygon grouping corruption.
Fresh-context reproduction confirmed duplicate metadata keys silently expand two boxes to three and sixteen vertices to twenty-four, while integer metadata keys fail character-integer joins.
Fresh-context reproduction confirmed custom or NULL rowname errors, NA identifiers for unnamed matrices, and an empty layer for duplicate cells because widening precedes aggregation.
Fresh-context reproduction confirmed nonzero origins are inconsistently applied, equal partitions return NULL gaps, and singleton adjustment can return infinite gaps.
Fresh-context reproduction confirmed internal-node labels can enter tip normalization and that geom_nodemarquee() fails without an explicit label mapping while the tip wrapper supplies one.

Fresh-context review confirmed no tests or CI, per-layer layout recomputation, manual five-panel composition, and user-managed ID ordering; it supported tests/CI, validated normalization, and one shared layout, but found insufficient evidence to make a high-level composer or speculative ecosystem features immediate Must items.
Two independently verified silent geometry-corruption defects and the absence of regression gates require a correctness-focused stabilization release before new features.
Verified public and opt-in input/layout defects converge on one canonical validation contract for identifiers, types, duplicates, metadata, tips, and finite layout parameters.
A shared validated layout and staged API cleanup are supported, while the composer is a post-stabilization Should and broader ecosystem or optimization features lack immediate demand evidence.

The current tarball smoke checks pass but omit tests and packaged vignettes; tidyverse guidance supports file-aligned tests, base pipes, concise documentation, and explicit internal/public boundaries.
